You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 

Your task is summarize the modifications made in the patch.
Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

From e0d4675789499b5955aa05ef9abc2926b30ba4ba Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Karel Zak <kzak@redhat.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Apr 2014 11:29:09 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] kill: fix bug in --all semantic

Introduces by 2ab6683f59cd3371b1c3ac8b5c248d5104ed4d41.

Signed-off-by: Karel Zak <kzak@redhat.com>

diff --git a/misc-utils/kill.c b/misc-utils/kill.c
index 37f4c6e34..d461b36a6 100644
--- a/misc-utils/kill.c
+++ b/misc-utils/kill.c
@@ -486,7 +486,7 @@ int main(int argc, char **argv)
 
 			if (!ps)
 				continue;
-			if (ctl.check_all)
+			if (!ctl.check_all)
 				proc_processes_filter_by_uid(ps, getuid());
 
 			proc_processes_filter_by_name(ps, ctl.arg);
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `misc-utils/kill.c`**
   - The condition checking for `ctl.check_all` was modified from `if (ctl.check_all)` to `if (!ctl.check_all)`. This change alters the logic to filter processes based on the user ID only when `check_all` is false, which is a correction to the previous behavior introduced in a prior commit.

### Relationships
- The modification in `kill.c` addresses a bug related to the `--all` option's semantics, which was introduced by a previous commit (identified by the hash `2ab6683f59cd3371b1c3ac8b5c248d5104ed4d41`). The change ensures that the process filtering logic behaves correctly depending on the state of `ctl.check_all`, thereby fixing the bug associated with the `--all` option.
